items.stem: A team needs operating-system-level control and a specific SQL Server version. Which Azure SQL option fits best?

options.text: SQL Server on Azure Virtual Machines
options.rationale: Correct: SQL Server on Azure VMs gives full OS and version control.
Azure SQL Database is PaaS and does not expose OS-level control.
Elastic pools are still PaaS without OS control.
Blob Storage is object storage, not a SQL database engine.

items.explanation: Correct: SQL Server on Azure VMs gives full OS-level and version control.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which TWO are deployment or purchasing options for Azure SQL Database? (Select TWO.)

options.rationale: Correct: an elastic pool is a deployment model sharing resources across databases.
Correct: serverless is a purchasing/compute option that autoscales and can pause.
Incorrect: Azure SQL Database is a cloud PaaS service.
Incorrect: backups are automated to Azure storage, not tape tiers.

items.explanation: Correct: elastic pools and the serverless tier are Azure SQL Database options.

items.stem: Which capability lets Azure SQL Database restore a database to any point in time within the retention period?

options.rationale: Correct: automatic backups enable point-in-time restore within the retention period.
Elastic pools share resources but do not themselves provide point-in-time restore.
The DTU model is a pricing abstraction, not a restore feature.
CSV exports are not the point-in-time restore mechanism.

items.explanation: Correct: automatic backups enable point-in-time restore within the retention period.
